![image_2026-10-05_222519479](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/e20ec0cdb7338dd9a1f3f31873e532c007e2c424502a9462589a3a2e43be1ec8.png)

Finally figured out KiCad(mostly, I still suck a bit)

So today was the first day using KiCad,I had to make Starbie on it. Initially I

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 212333](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/1cda410be9746ecdaae1b66aebcc1df4574edaf5078421eb0446df8f3a7d7fc6.png)

struggled quite a lot, but after the first hour of messing around on it, I finally figured it out.
So while figuring it out, I managed to make all the schematic parts of Starbie, I have the environment sensor left which I will do tomorrow.
It took a lot of time to figure how to do anything on KiCad ,but after figuring out(mainly through trial and error, and lots of random clicking) how, it was immensely satisfying to do things. It felt like playing with the circuit equivalent of Legos. It was great!

tl;dr is I spent the first day  figuring out how to wok on KiCad and find joy in working on it. It's just a matter of messing around a bit till everything starts making sense
